# kadr

> kadr is a declarative Swift library for composing, transforming and exporting video on Apple platforms (iOS 17, macOS 14, tvOS 17, visionOS 1). A result-builder DSL (`Video { … }`) describes the timeline, `async`/`await` runs the export, and nothing underneath it but AVFoundation. It needs Xcode 26 (Swift 6.2) and has no third-party dependencies.

Install with Swift Package Manager: `.package(url: "https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr.git", from: "1.2.1")`, product `Kadr`. kadr follows semantic versioning: nothing public breaks within 1.x.

A complete program:

```swift
import Kadr

let url = try await Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL).trimmed(to: 0...4)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(photo, duration: 3)
}
.overlay(TextOverlay("Hello", style: TextStyle(fontSize: 96, weight: .bold)).position(.bottom))
.audio(url: musicURL)
.preset(.cinema)          // 1920×1080, 24 fps. The default, .auto, is vertical 1080×1920.
.export(to: outputURL)
```

## Things that trip people up

- **The default output is vertical.** Without `.preset(_:)`, a video exports at 1080×1920. Use `.preset(.cinema)` for landscape 1920×1080, `.square` for 1080×1080, or `.custom(width:height:frameRate:codec:)`. Clips are scaled to fill the frame and centred.
- **`Transform` arguments go in declaration order**: `Transform(center:rotation:scale:anchor:)`, each optional. `Transform(scale: 0.5, center: …)` does not compile. Positions are `.normalized(x:y:)` from the top-left, 0...1.
- **Keyframe times are clip-relative.** A keyframe `.at(0.0, …)` is the clip's first frame, not the start of the video.
- **Speed takes a `Speed`.** `.speed(0.5)` works for a number literal, but a rate in a variable needs `.speed(.flat(rate))`. A changing rate is `.speed(.curved(animation))`. The range is 0.25 to 4.
- **Overlays don't export in the iOS Simulator.** Exports with text or image overlays throw `KadrError` there, because Core Animation export is broken on the Simulator. They work on devices and macOS. Previews are unaffected.
- **Transitions sit between two clips**, never first or last, and must be shorter than the clips beside them. A dissolve overlaps its clips, so it shortens the video; a fade does not.
- **`try` goes outside the builder.** Build a throwing value such as `try LUT(url:)` before `Video { … }` and use it inside.
- **Lists work inside `Video {}`**: `Video { urls.map { VideoClip(url: $0) } }`.

## Docs

- [Getting Started](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/GettingStarted.md): from adding the package to a previewed export with progress, cancellation and errors
- [Cookbook](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/Cookbook.md): seventeen "how do I…" recipes, each a few lines: merge, trim, crossfade, slideshow, music, mute, slow motion, reverse, text, watermark, picture-in-picture, green screen, filters and LUTs, crop, file size, thumbnails, subtitles
- [Keyframe Animation](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/KeyframeAnimation.md): animating transforms, opacity and filters over time
- [Multi-Track Composition](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/MultiTrackComposition.md): layers, picture-in-picture, named tracks
- [Slideshows](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/Slideshows.md): photos with Ken Burns motion and transitions
- [Custom Compositors](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/CustomCompositors.md): per-frame Core Image processing
- [Frame Accuracy](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/FrameAccuracy.md): times, rounding and frame boundaries
- [Known Platform Issues](https://steliyanh.github.io/kadr/articles/KnownPlatformIssues.md): Simulator limits and workarounds
- [API reference](https://swiftpackageindex.com/SteliyanH/kadr/documentation/kadr): every public type, hosted on the Swift Package Index
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteliyanH/kadr/main/README.md): recipes with the GIFs they render

## Companion packages

- [kadr-ui](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-ui): SwiftUI editor components: `VideoPreview`, `TimelineView`, `ThumbnailStrip`, `OverlayHost`, `InspectorPanel`, `KeyframeEditor`
- [kadr-captions](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-captions): parse and write SRT, WebVTT, iTT, ASS and SSA captions
- [kadr-photos](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-photos): Photos library assets as kadr clips, and a SwiftUI picker
- [kadr-audio](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-audio): music library tracks, voiceover recording, loudness measurement
- [kadr-persistence](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-persistence): save and open compositions

<!-- README.md -->

# Kadr

[![CI](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Swift versions](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fswiftpackageindex.com%2Fapi%2Fpackages%2FSteliyanH%2Fkadr%2Fbadge%3Ftype%3Dswift-versions)](https://swiftpackageindex.com/SteliyanH/kadr)
[![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fswiftpackageindex.com%2Fapi%2Fpackages%2FSteliyanH%2Fkadr%2Fbadge%3Ftype%3Dplatforms)](https://swiftpackageindex.com/SteliyanH/kadr)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-Buy%20me%20a%20coffee-FFDD00?logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/steliyanh)

**SwiftUI for video. Compose, transform, export — in Swift you actually want to write.**

A declarative Swift library for video on Apple platforms: a result-builder DSL,
async/await throughout, and nothing underneath but AVFoundation.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/media/hero.gif" width="560" alt="An illustrated coastline slowly zooms in under a bouncing &quot;kadr&quot; title, dissolves into a flight over mountains, and a talking cartoon face pops into the top-right corner.">
</p>

That video is the code below, rendered by kadr. Every GIF on this page comes
from the snippet printed beside it. They are re-rendered by
`swift run KadrReadmeMedia`, and CI compiles every snippet.

<!-- readme-snippet: hero -->
```swift
let video = Video {
    ImageClip(coast, duration: 4)
        .transform(.identity, animation: .keyframes([                 // Ken Burns
            .at(0.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.0)),
            .at(4.0, value: Transform(center: .normalized(x: 0.6, y: 0.45), scale: 1.3)),
        ], timing: .easeInOut))
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.8)
    VideoClip(url: droneURL).trimmed(to: 0...5)
    VideoClip(url: reactionURL).trimmed(to: 0...3)                    // picture-in-picture
        .at(time: 4.5)
        .transform(Transform(center: .normalized(x: 0.96, y: 0.06), scale: 0.32, anchor: .topRight))
}
.overlay(
    TextOverlay("kadr", style: TextStyle(fontSize: 240, alignment: .center, weight: .bold))
        .position(.center)
        .visible(during: 0.4...3.2)
        .animation(.scaleUp(duration: 0.6))
)
.audio(url: musicURL)
.preset(.cinema)

let url = try await video.export(to: outputURL)
```

## Quick Start

This needs no media files: `SampleMedia` draws its own frames. There are no
overlays either, so it also runs in the iOS Simulator.

```swift
import Kadr

let output = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("hello.mp4")

let url = try await Video {
    ImageClip(SampleMedia.image(index: 0), duration: 2)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(SampleMedia.image(index: 1), duration: 2)
}
.preset(.reelsAndShorts)          // 1080×1920, 30 fps
.export(to: output)
```

Call it from any async context: a SwiftUI `.task`, a test, or a Playground. To
use your own media, swap in `VideoClip(url:)` and `ImageClip(_:duration:)`.

## Installation

Add kadr to your `Package.swift`:

<!-- readme-snippets: skip -->
```swift
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr.git", from: "1.2.1")
]
```

Or in Xcode: **File › Add Package Dependencies…** and enter the repository URL.

**Requires** Xcode 26 or later (Swift 6.2), and iOS 17, macOS 14, tvOS 17 or
visionOS 1. Xcode 16 cannot build kadr: the image types it stores are only
`Sendable` in the Xcode 26 SDKs.

> **Known issue: overlays in the iOS Simulator.** Exports with text or image
> overlays throw on the iOS Simulator, because Core Animation export is broken
> there. They work on devices and on macOS. Details and workarounds:
> [Known Platform Issues](https://swiftpackageindex.com/SteliyanH/kadr/documentation/kadr/knownplatformissues).

## Recipes

Each recipe is under 20 lines. More are in [`Examples/`](Examples).

### Slideshow with music

<img src="docs/media/slideshow.gif" width="400" alt="Three illustrated landscapes, each slowly zooming in, dissolving into the next.">

<!-- readme-snippet: slideshow -->
```swift
let kenBurns = Animation<Transform>.keyframes([
    .at(0.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.0)),
    .at(3.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.15)),
])

let url = try await Video {
    ImageClip(coast, duration: 3).transform(.identity, animation: kenBurns)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.6)
    ImageClip(mountains, duration: 3).transform(.identity, animation: kenBurns)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.6)
    ImageClip(lake, duration: 3).transform(.identity, animation: kenBurns)
}
.audio(url: musicURL)
.preset(.cinema)
.export(to: outputURL)
```

### Vertical video for Reels, Shorts and TikTok

<img src="docs/media/vertical.gif" width="220" alt="Landscape mountain footage reframed to a tall 9:16 video with a title at the top.">

<!-- readme-snippet: vertical -->
```swift
// Landscape footage in, 1080×1920 out: the clip is scaled to fill the frame.
let url = try await Video {
    VideoClip(url: droneURL).trimmed(to: 0...6)
}
.overlay(
    TextOverlay("Above the Alps", style: TextStyle(fontSize: 104, alignment: .center,
                                                   weight: .bold, shadow: TextShadow()))
        .position(.normalized(x: 0.5, y: 0.14))
)
.preset(.reelsAndShorts)
.export(to: outputURL)
```

### Picture-in-picture reaction

<img src="docs/media/pip.gif" width="400" alt="Mountain footage with a small talking cartoon face in the top-right corner.">

<!-- readme-snippet: pip -->
```swift
let url = try await Video {
    VideoClip(url: droneURL).trimmed(to: 0...6)
    VideoClip(url: reactionURL).trimmed(to: 0...5)      // a second layer, from 0.5 s
        .at(time: 0.5)
        .transform(Transform(center: .normalized(x: 0.96, y: 0.06), scale: 0.35, anchor: .topRight))
}
.preset(.cinema)
.export(to: outputURL)
```

### Green screen

<img src="docs/media/greenScreen.gif" width="400" alt="A waving cartoon presenter, filmed on green, standing in front of a dusk landscape.">

<!-- readme-snippet: greenScreen -->
```swift
let url = try await Video {
    ImageClip(dusk, duration: 5)                        // the backdrop
    VideoClip(url: presenterURL)                        // filmed on green
        .filter(.chromaKey(color: .green, threshold: 0.35))
        .at(time: 0)
}
.preset(.cinema)
.export(to: outputURL)
```

### Speed ramp

<img src="docs/media/speedRamp.gif" width="400" alt="A ball rolling across a field slows to a crawl, then speeds past the fence posts.">

<!-- readme-snippet: speedRamp -->
```swift
let ramp = Animation<Double>.keyframes([
    .at(0.0, value: 1.0),
    .at(1.2, value: 0.25),      // into slow motion…
    .at(2.4, value: 2.0),       // …then double speed
    .at(4.0, value: 1.0),
])

let url = try await Video {
    VideoClip(url: rollURL).speed(.curved(ramp))
}
.preset(.cinema)
.export(to: outputURL)
```

### Animated titles

<img src="docs/media/titles.gif" width="400" alt="Mountain footage with a bold outlined title sliding in from the left, then a subtitle fading in under it.">

<!-- readme-snippet: titles -->
```swift
let title = TextStyle(fontSize: 132, weight: .bold, stroke: TextStroke(width: 4), shadow: TextShadow(blur: 8))
let subtitle = TextStyle(fontSize: 64, weight: .medium, shadow: TextShadow(blur: 6))

let url = try await Video {
    VideoClip(url: droneURL).trimmed(to: 0...5)
}
.overlay(
    TextOverlay("Chapter one", style: title)
        .position(.normalized(x: 0.06, y: 0.72)).anchor(.bottomLeft)
        .visible(during: 0.3...5.0)
        .animation(.slideIn(from: .fromLeft, duration: 0.6))
)
.overlay(
    TextOverlay("The long way up", style: subtitle)
        .position(.normalized(x: 0.06, y: 0.82)).anchor(.bottomLeft)
        .visible(during: 1.0...5.0)
        .animation(.fadeIn(duration: 0.6))
)
.preset(.cinema)
.export(to: outputURL)
```

## Why kadr?

FFmpegKit retired in January 2025. Pixel SDK sunset in February 2025. AVFoundation is powerful but verbose. The Swift video ecosystem needs a modern, native, declarative library.

Here is a 9:16 export of one clip in kadr. If the camera stored the clip
rotated, kadr turns it upright, then scales it to fill the frame and centres it:

<!-- readme-snippet: kadrVertical -->
```swift
let url = try await Video { VideoClip(url: droneURL).trimmed(to: 0...6) }
    .preset(.reelsAndShorts)
    .export(to: outputURL)
```

And here is the same export in AVFoundation. `swift run KadrReadmeMedia`
runs both and checks that their frames match.

<details>
<summary><b>The same export in raw AVFoundation: 40 lines</b></summary>

<!-- readme-snippet: rawAVFoundation -->
```swift
func exportVertical(source: URL, to output: URL) async throws {
    let asset = AVURLAsset(url: source)
    let composition = AVMutableComposition()
    let range = CMTimeRange(start: .zero, duration: CMTime(seconds: 6, preferredTimescale: 600))

    guard let sourceVideo = try await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .video).first,
          let video = composition.addMutableTrack(withMediaType: .video,
                                                  preferredTrackID: kCMPersistentTrackID_Invalid)
    else { throw CocoaError(.fileReadCorruptFile) }
    try video.insertTimeRange(range, of: sourceVideo, at: .zero)

    if let sourceAudio = try await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio).first,
       let audio = composition.addMutableTrack(withMediaType: .audio,
                                               preferredTrackID: kCMPersistentTrackID_Invalid) {
        try audio.insertTimeRange(range, of: sourceAudio, at: .zero)
    }

    // Turn the frame upright, scale it to fill 1080×1920, and centre it.
    let renderSize = CGSize(width: 1080, height: 1920)
    let (naturalSize, preferred) = try await sourceVideo.load(.naturalSize, .preferredTransform)
    let upright = CGRect(origin: .zero, size: naturalSize).applying(preferred)
    let scale = max(renderSize.width / upright.width, renderSize.height / upright.height)
    let transform = preferred
        .concatenating(CGAffineTransform(translationX: -upright.minX, y: -upright.minY))
        .concatenating(CGAffineTransform(scaleX: scale, y: scale))
        .concatenating(CGAffineTransform(translationX: (renderSize.width - upright.width * scale) / 2,
                                         y: (renderSize.height - upright.height * scale) / 2))

    let layer = AVMutableVideoCompositionLayerInstruction(assetTrack: video)
    layer.setTransform(transform, at: .zero)
    let instruction = AVMutableVideoCompositionInstruction()
    instruction.timeRange = range
    instruction.layerInstructions = [layer]
    let videoComposition = AVMutableVideoComposition()
    videoComposition.renderSize = renderSize
    videoComposition.frameDuration = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: 30)
    videoComposition.instructions = [instruction]

    guard let session = AVAssetExportSession(asset: composition,
                                             presetName: AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality)
    else { throw CocoaError(.featureUnsupported) }
    session.videoComposition = videoComposition
    try await session.export(to: output, as: .mp4)
}

try await exportVertical(source: droneURL, to: outputURL)
```

</details>

### Compared with the alternatives

| | Kadr | AVFoundation (raw) | VideoLab | FFmpegKit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **API style** | Declarative DSL | Imperative | Layer-based | CLI wrapper |
| **Swift concurrency** | async/await native | Callbacks | No | No |
| **Swift 6 / Sendable** | Full strict concurrency | Partial | No | No |
| **Maintained (2026)** | Active | Apple (low-level) | Inactive | Retired (Jan 2025) |
| **Dependencies** | None (AVFoundation only) | N/A | None | FFmpeg binary |
| **Learning curve** | Minutes | Hours | Hours | Moderate |
| **License** | Apache 2.0 | Proprietary | MIT | LGPL |

## Features

Everything below is in the shipping public API. For what changed in which
release, see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) — it is not duplicated here, so it
cannot drift out of date here either.

**Composition**
- Result-builder DSL over `Video`, `Track`, `VideoClip`, `ImageClip` and `TitleSequence`, `async`/`await` throughout, no third-party dependencies.
- Multi-track timelines with named lanes and per-track opacity; time-anchored audio tracks.
- `KadrVideoCompositor` for custom per-frame compositing, and `makePlayerItem()` so a composition previews before it exports.

**Transform and animation**
- `Transform(center:rotation:scale:anchor:)` on every clip type — picture-in-picture, scaled cutaways, rotated clips.
- `Animation<T>` with `Animatable` conformances for `Transform`, `Double`, `Position` and `Size`. `TimingFunction` covers linear, ease-in/out, cubic Bézier and custom closures.
- **Keyframes are clip-relative**: a keyframe at `0.0` maps to the clip's first frame, not composition zero. The same animations drive export and live preview.

**Filters**
- Animatable presets including brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, sepia, gaussian blur, vignette, sharpen, zoom blur and glow.
- Keyed by `FilterID`, so animations bound to a filter survive reordering instead of drifting onto their neighbours.

**Overlays and text**
- `TextOverlay` with built-in animation recipes (`.fadeIn`, `.slideIn`, `.scaleUp`), plus `ImageOverlay` and `StickerOverlay` with animatable position and size.
- `TextStyle` carries `TextStroke` and `TextShadow` — legible copy over busy footage.

**Audio**
- Per-track volume, fades, ducking, `volumeRamp(start:end:during:)` and declaration-ordered `crossfade(_:)`.
- Pitch-preserving speed from 0.25× to 4× via `AudioTimePitchAlgorithm` (`.spectral`, `.timeDomain`, `.varispeed`).

**Timing**
- `Speed` is `.flat(Double)` or `.curved(Animation<Double>)`, so a clip is one or the other at compile time. A number literal is a flat rate: `.speed(0.5)` is half speed. Curved rates are integrated into a piecewise-linear time map that audio follows.

**Captions**
- `Caption` value type and `Video.captions(_:)` bake cues as an `AVMetadataItem` group at export. File parsing for SRT, VTT, iTT, ASS and SSA lives in [`kadr-captions`](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-captions); the core stays a bridge.

**Export**
- `ThumbnailGenerator` reuses one `AVAssetImageGenerator` across many frame requests, with a batch `AsyncThrowingStream` for filmstrips and cooperative `cancel()`.
- `CancellationToken` backed by real synchronisation, not an unchecked claim.

### Roadmap

See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for the full version plan.

## Companion packages

Kadr is the engine. Five packages consume its public
surface for specific jobs — pull in only what you need; none are required for
composition or export.

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`kadr-ui`](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-ui) | SwiftUI components — `VideoPreview`, `ThumbnailStrip`, multi-lane `TimelineView` (selection / reorder / trim / scrub / audio waveforms), `OverlayHost` with gesture-routed `LayerID` hit-testing, `InspectorPanel` with filter authoring, `TransitionPicker`, `ClipSplitter`, `KeyframeEditor`. |
| [`kadr-persistence`](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-persistence) | Save a composition to a file and open it again — refusing, rather than silently dropping, whatever a file cannot hold. Content-addressed image storage; a completeness guard that fails when kadr grows a field. |
| [`kadr-audio`](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-audio) | Music-library resolution, in-app voiceover recording, audio session policy, and ITU-R BS.1770-4 (LUFS) loudness measurement. |
| [`kadr-captions`](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-captions) | Caption parsing and authoring for SRT, VTT, iTT, ASS and SSA, plus a styled-VTT bridge onto `TextOverlay` + `textAnimation` for burned-in animated captions. |
| [`kadr-photos`](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-photos) | Photos library integration — resolves video / image / Live Photo `PHAsset`s into kadr clip types, wraps `PHPickerViewController` for SwiftUI, bridges assets to `ImageOverlay` / `StickerOverlay`. |

And a reference application: [**Kadr Studio**](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-reels-studio),
a short-form vertical video editor built on all six.

## API stability

From **v1.0.0**, kadr follows semantic versioning without asterisks:

- **No breaking change without a major bump.** Nothing public is removed,
  renamed, or given a different meaning inside `1.x`.
- **Minors add.** New filters, new modifiers, new overlay kinds — all additive,
  all source-compatible.
- **Deprecation before removal.** Anything on its way out is marked
  `@available(*, deprecated:)` for at least one minor with a named replacement,
  and can only actually disappear in a major.

What this does *not* promise: `internal` symbols, the exact bytes an export
produces (encoders change under us), and performance figures — those are tracked
as a regression baseline in [`Benchmarks/README.md`](Benchmarks/README.md), not
as a contract.

## Platform Support

| Platform | Minimum Version |
|---|---|
| iOS | 17.0 |
| macOS | 14.0 |
| tvOS | 17.0 |
| visionOS | 1.0 |

## Architecture

Kadr separates the public DSL from the internal engine:

- **DSL layer** *(public, semver-stable)* — `Video`, `Track`, `VideoClip`, `ImageClip`, `TitleSequence`, `Transition`, `AudioTrack`, `Preset`, `Exporter`, `Filter`, `Animation<T>`, `Transform`, plus the overlay / compositor / animation surfaces.
- **Engine layer** *(internal, uses AVFoundation)* — `CompositionBuilder` (timeline assembly + multi-track routing), `FilterProcessor` (per-frame `CIFilter` pre-render with intensity animation), `KadrVideoCompositor` (custom `AVVideoCompositing` for multi-input compositors), `OverlayRenderer` (CALayer tree for `AVVideoCompositionCoreAnimationTool`), `PlaybackComposer` (`AVPlayerItem` for previews), `ExportEngine` (`AVAssetExportSession` driver), `ImageEncoder` (still-image fast path), `ReverseProcessor`.

The DSL is the stable public API. The engine is the implementation detail that can be refactored without breaking semver.

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/GettingStarted.md -->

# Getting Started

Add kadr to an app, build a video, preview it, and export it.

## Overview

A kadr video is a value. You describe it with ``Video`` and a result builder,
the way you describe a SwiftUI view, and nothing is read or rendered until you
preview or export it. This article goes from an empty project to an exported
file in five steps.

## Add the package

In Xcode, choose **File › Add Package Dependencies…** and enter
`https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr.git`. In a `Package.swift`:

<!-- readme-snippets: skip -->
```swift
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr.git", from: "1.2.1")
]
```

kadr needs Xcode 26 (Swift 6.2) and runs on iOS 17, macOS 14, tvOS 17 and
visionOS 1 or later.

## Make a first video

This needs no media files: ``SampleMedia`` draws its own frames.

```swift
let output = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("first.mp4")

let url = try await Video {
    ImageClip(SampleMedia.image(index: 0), duration: 2)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(SampleMedia.image(index: 1), duration: 2)
}
.preset(.reelsAndShorts)          // 1080×1920, 30 fps
.export(to: output)
```

``Video/export(to:)`` is `async` and throws, so call it from a SwiftUI `.task`,
a `Task`, or an `async` test. It returns the URL of the finished file.

## Use your own media

``VideoClip`` takes a file URL and ``ImageClip`` takes an image and a duration.
Clips play one after another, and a ``Transition`` between two clips blends
them:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL).trimmed(to: 2...8)    // seconds 2 to 8 of the file
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(photo, duration: 3)
}
.audio(url: musicURL)
.preset(.cinema)
```

Reading from the Photos library or a picker? The
[kadr-photos](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-photos) package turns a
`PHAsset` or a picker result into these clips.

## Preview before you export

``Video/makePlayerItem()`` builds an `AVPlayerItem` that plays the
composition live, without writing a file:

```swift
struct PreviewView: View {
    let video: Video
    @State private var player: AVPlayer?

    var body: some View {
        VideoPlayer(player: player)
            .task {
                if let item = try? await video.makePlayerItem() {
                    player = AVPlayer(playerItem: item)
                }
            }
    }
}
```

For a timeline, trim handles and overlays you can drag, use
[kadr-ui](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-ui).

## Show progress, and let people cancel

``Video/export(to:)`` waits for the whole file. For a progress bar, ask for an
``Exporter`` and read its updates:

```swift
let exporter = video.exporter(to: outputURL)

do {
    for try await progress in exporter.run() {
        print("\(Int(progress.fractionCompleted * 100))%")
    }
} catch KadrError.cancelled {
    // exporter.cancel() was called, from a Cancel button for example.
}
```

## Handle errors

Every error kadr throws is a ``KadrError``. Its `localizedDescription` is
written for the person using your app, and `recoverySuggestion` says what to do
about it:

```swift
do {
    let file = try await video.export(to: outputURL)
    print(file)
} catch let error as KadrError {
    print(error.localizedDescription, error.recoverySuggestion ?? "")
}
```

Exports with overlays fail on the iOS Simulator. They work on devices and on
macOS. See <doc:KnownPlatformIssues>.

## Next steps

- <doc:Cookbook> answers the common "how do I…" questions in a few lines each.
- <doc:Slideshows>, <doc:MultiTrackComposition> and <doc:KeyframeAnimation>
  go deeper into one topic each.

---

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/Cookbook.md -->

# Cookbook

Short answers to the common "how do I…" questions about video on Apple
platforms.

## Overview

Each recipe is a complete composition. Export any of them with
`try await video.export(to: outputURL)`, or preview one with
``Video/makePlayerItem()``. <doc:GettingStarted> covers both.

## Combining and cutting

### How do I merge several videos into one?

List the clips. They play in order, and each is scaled to fill the output frame
and centred, so their sizes need not match:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: a)
    VideoClip(url: b)
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.preset(.cinema)       // 1920×1080
```

Set the preset to the shape you want. Without one the output is vertical,
1080×1920, and landscape clips lose their sides to fill it.

### How do I trim a video?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL).trimmed(to: 2...8)    // keep seconds 2 to 8
}
```

For frame-exact cuts, pass a `CMTimeRange` instead. See <doc:FrameAccuracy>.

### How do I crossfade between two clips?

Put a ``Transition`` between them:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: a)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.75)
    VideoClip(url: b)
}
```

A dissolve overlaps the two clips, so the video is shorter than the clips laid
end to end by the dissolve's length. A transition must be shorter than both of
the clips it joins, and cannot come first or last.

### How do I make a slideshow from photos?

```swift
let video = Video {
    ImageClip(first, duration: 3)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(second, duration: 3)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(third, duration: 3)
}
.audio(url: musicURL)
```

<doc:Slideshows> adds slow zooms, title cards and fitting the music.

## Sound

### How do I add background music?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.audio {
    AudioTrack(url: musicURL)
        .volume(0.6)
        .fadeIn(1)
        .fadeOut(2)
        .ducking(0.25)     // quieter while the clip's own sound plays
}
```

### How do I mute a clip, or replace its sound?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: a).muted()                    // silent
    VideoClip(url: b).withAudio(musicURL)        // this file's sound instead
}
```

`withAudio` is cut to the clip's length and does not loop.

## Speed

### How do I make slow motion or a time-lapse?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: a).speed(0.5)      // half speed
    VideoClip(url: b).speed(4)        // four times as fast
}
```

The rate must be between 0.25 and 4. For a speed that changes during the clip,
pass a curve: `.speed(.curved(animation))`.

### How do I play a clip backwards?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL).trimmed(to: 0...3).reversed()
}
```

kadr writes the reversed frames to a temporary file first, so keep reversed
clips short.

## Text and images on top

### How do I put text on a video?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.overlay(
    TextOverlay("Day one", style: TextStyle(fontSize: 96, weight: .bold, shadow: TextShadow()))
        .position(.normalized(x: 0.5, y: 0.85))
        .visible(during: 0.5...4)
        .animation(.fadeIn(duration: 0.4))
)
```

`fontSize` is in pixels of the exported video, so a size looks the same at
every preview size.

### How do I add a logo or watermark?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.overlay(
    ImageOverlay(logo)
        .size(.aspectFit(within: .normalized(width: 0.2, height: 0.1),
                         sourceAspect: logo.size.width / logo.size.height))
        .position(.normalized(x: 0.96, y: 0.96))
        .anchor(.bottomRight)
        .opacity(0.8)
)
```

`.anchor(.bottomRight)` puts the logo's corner, not its centre, at the
position, so it sits just inside the frame's corner.

### How do I show one video in a corner of another?

Give the second clip a start time with `.at(time:)`. It then plays on a layer
above the first instead of after it:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: main)
    VideoClip(url: inset)
        .at(time: 1)
        .transform(Transform(center: .normalized(x: 0.96, y: 0.04), scale: 0.3, anchor: .topRight))
}
```

<doc:MultiTrackComposition> covers layers and tracks.

### How do I remove a green screen?

```swift
let video = Video {
    ImageClip(photo, duration: 5)                   // what shows through
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)                         // filmed on green
        .filter(.chromaKey(color: .green, threshold: 0.35))
        .at(time: 0)
}
```

## Look

### How do I apply a filter or a colour grade?

```swift
let grade = try LUT(url: lutURL)                              // a .cube file

let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: a).filter(.saturation(0))                  // black and white
    VideoClip(url: b).filter(.contrast(1.1), .vignette())
    VideoClip(url: clipURL).filter(.lut(grade))
}
```

### How do I crop to a square?

Pick the shape with the output preset. Each clip is scaled to fill it and
centred:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.preset(.square)
```

For a vertical video, use `.reelsAndShorts`, which is 1080×1920. To choose
which part of the frame to keep, use ``Video/crop(at:size:anchor:)``.

## Export

### How do I keep the file under a size limit?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.quality(.fileSize(bytes: 8_000_000))     // aim for 8 MB
```

kadr picks the bitrate from the video's duration. The result lands close to the
target, but not exactly on it.

### How do I get a thumbnail?

```swift
let cover = try await Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.thumbnail(at: 1.5)                       // the frame at 1.5 seconds
```

### How do I add subtitles?

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: clipURL)
}
.captions([
    Caption(text: "Hello", timeRange: CMTimeRange(start: .zero, duration: CMTime(value: 2, timescale: 1))),
])
```

These are a subtitle track that players can turn on and off. To read `.srt`
or `.vtt` files, or to draw captions into the picture, use
[kadr-captions](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr-captions).

---

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/CustomCompositors.md -->

# Custom Compositors

Running your own per-frame code, and the three constraints that shape it.

## Overview

``Compositor`` is the escape hatch. Filters cover the common adjustments; a
compositor runs arbitrary Core Image work on every frame of a clip, which is what
you need for effects the filter set does not name.

It is also the easiest place in this API to write something that works and is
unusably slow, so the constraints are worth understanding before the syntax.

## The closure form

For anything stateless, pass a closure:

```swift
let blurred = VideoClip(url: url).compositor { image, context in
    image.applyingFilter("CIGaussianBlur", parameters: [
        kCIInputRadiusKey: 8.0
    ])
}
```

``CompositorContext`` carries the frame's composition ``CompositorContext/time``
and the engine's ``CompositorContext/renderSize`` in pixels, post-crop and
post-preset. Time is what makes an effect animate:

```swift
let focusPull = VideoClip(url: url).compositor { image, context in
    let radius = min(20.0, context.time.seconds * 4.0)
    return image.applyingFilter("CIGaussianBlur", parameters: [kCIInputRadiusKey: radius])
}
```

## The protocol form

When the effect needs setup, conform a type instead. Anything expensive belongs
in the initialiser, not in `process`. Here the expensive part is a 32×32×32
colour table, built once and then applied to every frame:

```swift
struct WarmGrade: Compositor {
    private let cube: Data          // built once, read by every frame

    init(warmth: Float) {
        let size = 32, top = Float(size - 1)
        var table: [Float] = []
        table.reserveCapacity(size * size * size * 4)
        for blue in 0..<size {
            for green in 0..<size {
                for red in 0..<size {
                    table += [
                        min(1, Float(red) / top + warmth),
                        Float(green) / top,
                        max(0, Float(blue) / top - warmth),
                        1,
                    ]
                }
            }
        }
        cube = table.withUnsafeBufferPointer { Data(buffer: $0) }
    }

    func process(image: CIImage, context: CompositorContext) -> CIImage {
        image.applyingFilter("CIColorCube", parameters: [
            "inputCubeDimension": 32,
            "inputCubeData": cube,
        ])
    }
}

let graded = VideoClip(url: url).compositor(WarmGrade(warmth: 0.08))
```

Keep what you store immutable. A `CIFilter` is a mutable object, so a stored
one that `process` configures per frame is shared state, and Swift 6 rejects it
in a `Sendable` type. Store the inputs (numbers, `Data`, a `CIImage`) and call
`applyingFilter` in `process`; creating the filter there is cheap.

## The three constraints

**`process` is synchronous.** The engine wraps the call in
`applyingCIFiltersWithHandler`, which expects a non-`async` handler. There is no
place to await, and that is deliberate: per-frame `async` multiplies with frame
rate and duration, so a 5-second clip at 30 fps would suspend 150 times.

**It must be `Sendable`.** The engine crosses actor boundaries while running
compositors. Capture value types; do not reach for a shared mutable cache.

**Cost multiplies by frame count.** A 10 ms operation is invisible in isolation,
yet adds 1.5 seconds to a 5-second export at 30 fps and 18 seconds to a
one-minute one. Build tables and images once at construction, and prefer
`applyingFilter` chains over building images by hand.

## Order

Filters run first, then compositors, in declaration order. Both happen in the
same `applyingCIFiltersWithHandler` pass, so adding a compositor to a clip that
already has filters costs no extra encode.

Reversal, if present, happens before either — so a compositor sees frames in
their final playback order, not the source's.

## Multi-input work

``Compositor`` is single-input: one image in, one image out. Blending two
sources — a custom transition, a chroma composite over a second clip — needs
``MultiInputCompositor``, which is a separate protocol on the lower-level
`AVVideoCompositing` path and is applied to the composition rather than to a
clip.

## See Also

- ``Compositor``
- ``CompositorContext``
- ``MultiInputCompositor``
- ``Filter``
- <doc:MultiTrackComposition>

---

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/FrameAccuracy.md -->

# Frame Accuracy

How Kadr represents time, and when to reach for `CMTime` over `TimeInterval`.

## Overview

Every time-related value in Kadr's API has two forms:

- **`CMTime`** — frame-accurate. Stores time as a rational `value / timescale` so values like
  *1 frame at 30 fps* are exact (`CMTime(value: 1, timescale: 30)`).
- **`TimeInterval`** — ergonomic. A plain `Double` measured in seconds. Convenient for
  literal call sites like `0.5` or `0...10`, but inherently lossy for sub-second precision
  (`1.0 / 30.0 = 0.03333…`, never exactly 1/30).

`CMTime` is the type stored internally and the type used by AVFoundation throughout. The
`TimeInterval` overloads exist as static factory methods that bridge to `CMTime` at
construction. Engine math operates entirely in `CMTime`.

## When to use which

Use `CMTime` when:

- You're targeting a specific frame rate and want trims, fades, or transitions aligned to
  frame boundaries.
- You're seeking to or extracting thumbnails at exact frame positions.
- You're composing values you've read from AVFoundation (asset durations, track frame rates).

Use `TimeInterval` for everything else — readable literals, prototyping, anywhere a
fractional second of slop is acceptable.

```swift
// Frame-accurate (CMTime):
let exact = clip.trimmed(to: CMTimeRange(
    start:    CMTime(value: 30, timescale: 30),    // exactly second 1
    duration: CMTime(value: 90, timescale: 30)     // exactly 3 seconds
))
let oneFrame = Transition.fade(duration: CMTime(value: 1, timescale: 30))   // exactly 1 frame at 30fps

// Ergonomic (TimeInterval):
let roughly = clip.trimmed(to: 0...3)                         // close enough
let halfSecond = Transition.fade(duration: 0.5)               // close enough
```

## Wall-clock time vs media-timeline time

Not every duration is a media-timeline value. Kadr distinguishes:

- **Media-timeline time** — positions and durations within the composition. Frame-accurate.
  Always `CMTime`. (Examples: ``Transition`` durations, ``VideoClip/trimmed(to:)-(CMTimeRange)``,
  ``Video/duration``, ``Clip/duration``.)
- **Wall-clock time** — elapsed seconds in the real world. Frame accuracy doesn't apply.
  Always `TimeInterval`. (Example: ``ExportProgress/estimatedTimeRemaining`` — how long the
  user must wait for the export to finish.)

If you're holding a value, ask yourself: *does it move when the user pauses playback?*
If yes, it's media time → `CMTime`. If no, it's wall-clock time → `TimeInterval`.

## Engine guarantees

The composition engine performs all arithmetic in `CMTime`. Specifically:

- Fade halving uses `CMTimeMultiplyByRatio(d, multiplier: 1, divisor: 2)` — exact rational
  halving with no float drift.
- Validation comparisons use `CMTimeCompare` directly, not seconds-based `Double` comparisons.
- Trim ranges are stored and consumed as `CMTimeRange` — no round-tripping through `Double`.
- The single unavoidable `Double` touch is in ``VideoClip/speed(_:)`` (since the rate is a
  `Double` ratio); it uses `CMTimeMultiplyByFloat64` and is otherwise contained.

## Topics

### Time-related symbols

- ``Transition``
- ``VideoClip/trimmed(to:)-(CMTimeRange)``
- ``VideoClip/thumbnail(at:)-(CMTime)``
- ``ImageClip/init(_:duration:)-(_,CMTime)``
- ``AudioTrack/fadeIn(_:)-(CMTime)``
- ``AudioTrack/fadeOut(_:)-(CMTime)``

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/KeyframeAnimation.md -->

# Keyframe Animation

Driving a property over a clip's lifetime.

## Overview

Most of Kadr's per-clip properties have an animated form: give the modifier a
base value and an ``Animation``, and the engine samples it per frame.

The shape is the same everywhere — build the keyframes, hand them to the
modifier — so learning it once covers transforms, opacity and filter intensity.

## Building an animation

``Animation/keyframes(_:timing:)`` takes values at times. Keyframes are sorted on
construction, so out-of-order input is safe:

```swift
let fade = Animation<Double>.keyframes([
    .at(0.0, value: 0.0),
    .at(1.0, value: 1.0),
    .at(4.0, value: 1.0),
    .at(5.0, value: 0.0),
], timing: .linear)
```

Times are **clip-relative**, not composition-relative. A keyframe at `0.0` is the
start of the clip it is attached to, wherever that clip sits in the timeline —
which is what lets the same animation be reused across clips.

## Applying it

```swift
let clip = VideoClip(url: url).opacity(1.0, animation: fade)
```

The first argument is the base: the value used outside the animation's range.
Inside the range the animation wins. A base of `1.0` with the fade above means
the clip is fully opaque before the first keyframe and after the last, which is
usually what you want for a fade that only covers part of a longer clip.

## Animating a transform

``Transform`` animates as a whole, so position, scale and rotation move together:

```swift
let drift = Animation<Transform>.keyframes([
    .at(0.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.0)),
    .at(4.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.15)),
])

let clip = ImageClip(photo, duration: 4.0)
    .transform(Transform(scale: 1.0), animation: drift)
```

## Animating a filter

Filters animate their primary scalar — brightness, contrast, saturation,
exposure, sepia intensity. Filters without one (`.mono`, `.lut`, `.chromaKey`)
ignore the animation rather than failing:

```swift
let ramp = Animation<Double>.keyframes([
    .at(0.0, value: 0.0),
    .at(2.0, value: 0.6),
])

let clip = VideoClip(url: url).filter(.brightness(0.0), animation: ramp)
```

### Prefer the keyed surface

When a clip carries several filters and you need to change one later, address it
by ``FilterID`` rather than by index:

```swift
let clip = VideoClip(url: url).filter(.brightness(0.2))
let id = clip.filterIDs[0]

let animated = clip.filterAnimation(for: id, ramp)
let brighter = animated.setFilter(for: id, .brightness(0.5))   // keeps the animation
```

Index-based access drifts as soon as a filter is added or removed. The keyed
surface exists because that drift is silent — and until v0.18 appending a filter
regenerated every id, orphaning exactly these bindings.

## Timing

``TimingFunction`` shapes interpolation between keyframes. `.linear` is the
default and is the right choice more often than it looks: eased motion on a
2-second clip is largely indistinguishable from linear, and easing is most
visible on long, slow moves.

## See Also

- ``Animation``
- ``TimingFunction``
- ``Transform``
- ``FilterID``
- <doc:Slideshows>

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/KnownPlatformIssues.md -->

# Known Platform Issues

Apple platform bugs that affect Kadr compositions, what they look like, and how to work
around them.

## Overview

These are bugs in AVFoundation or Core Animation, not in Kadr. Each one reproduces with
plain AVFoundation code. Kadr works around the ones it can; the ones listed here it
currently can't, so they're documented with a workaround instead.

Both issues below affect the **iOS Simulator only**. Real devices and macOS are not
affected.

## Overlay exports fail on the iOS Simulator

**Affects:** exports with any overlay (``TextOverlay``, ``ImageOverlay``,
``StickerOverlay``, ``Video/watermark(_:position:size:opacity:)``) on the iOS 26.5 and 27.0
Simulators. Previews are not affected: they don't use the export overlay path.

**What Kadr does:** on the iOS Simulator, ``Video/export(to:)`` with overlays throws
``KadrError/exportFailed(underlying:)``, with a message pointing here. It refuses before
rendering anything, because the underlying failure kills the app and can't be caught.

**The underlying bug:** without that check, the app crashes during export with
`EXC_BREAKPOINT` and the crash report signature *API Misuse*. The crashing thread is on
the `com.apple.coremedia.basicvideocompositor.output` queue:

```
_xpc_api_misuse
_xpc_shmem_create_with_prot
_ioSurfaceClientCreate
IOSurfaceCreate
CA::Render::Image::retain_iosurface() const
CA::OGL::GLESContext::retain_image(...)
...
-[CARenderer render]
FigCoreAnimationRendererCopyPixelBufferAtTime
```

This reproduces with plain AVFoundation, in an app as well as in tests.

**Cause:** overlays are drawn by `AVVideoCompositionCoreAnimationTool`, which renders
each video frame through Core Animation. On the Simulator, AVFoundation's video frames
are ordinary `malloc` memory rather than IOSurfaces. Core Animation tries to wrap that
memory in an IOSurface, and libxpc rejects it with *"Attempt to pass a malloc(3)ed region
to xpc_shmem_create()"*, which is a deliberate trap rather than an error. The same export
completes when the frames are IOSurface-backed.

**Workaround:** export compositions with overlays on a device or on macOS. If your app
must export on the Simulator during development, leave the overlays out of
Simulator builds:

```swift
var video = Video { VideoClip(url: clipURL) }
#if !targetEnvironment(simulator)
video = video.overlay(TextOverlay("Title"))
#endif
```

## Transition previews stall on the iOS Simulator

**Affects:** preview playback (``Video/makePlayerItem()``) of a composition with a
transition, on the iOS 26 Simulator, when the source clips' resolution exactly equals the
preset's render size. Export is not affected.
([#203](https://github.com/SteliyanH/kadr/issues/203))

**Symptom:** playback stops at the first transition. The player item posts
`AVPlayerItemFailedToPlayToEndTime` with error `-11800`, underlying `-19230`
("CoreAnimation image queue does not support this pixel format").

**Cause:** when the decoded frame already matches the render size, the Simulator's
display pipeline passes it straight to Core Animation's image queue, which supports
fewer pixel formats on the Simulator than on a device.

**Workaround:** for Simulator builds only, nudge the render size by half a point after
building the player item. `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is copied on set, so mutate a
copy and assign it back:

```swift
let item = try await video.makePlayerItem()
#if targetEnvironment(simulator)
if let composition = item.videoComposition?.mutableCopy() as? AVMutableVideoComposition {
    composition.renderSize.width += 0.5
    item.videoComposition = composition
}
#endif
```

---

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/MigrationGuide.md -->

# Migrating to 1.0

What changed across the `0.x` line, and which changes your compiler will not
catch.

## Overview

**There has been no breaking change since v0.14.0.** Releases since have added
API — per-clip volume in 0.18, waveform extraction moving into core in 0.18/0.19,
export quality and sample media in 0.20 — but nothing has been removed or had its
meaning changed. If you are on 0.14 or later, upgrading to 1.0 requires no source
changes at all, only a version-range edit.

If you are on an earlier version, this guide lists every breaking change in
order. Most are one-line mechanical edits that fail to compile until fixed.

**The ones worth your attention are at the end.** A change that stops your code
compiling announces itself. A change that alters what your code *does* while
still compiling does not, and there are three of those.

## First: fix your version range

This applies to every consumer regardless of version, and it is the change most
likely to bite silently.

<!-- readme-snippets: skip -->
```swift
// Wrong, and probably what you have
.package(url: "...kadr.git", from: "0.14.0")

// Right, until 1.0
.package(url: "...kadr.git", .upToNextMinor(from: "0.21.0"))
```

`from:` means `.upToNextMajor`, and **SwiftPM does not special-case `0.x`**. So
`from: "0.14.0"` accepts every later 0.x release — including the ones on this
page that removed API. A pre-1.0 dependency pinned with `from:` will eventually
break on an update you did not ask for.

At 1.0 this inverts: `from: "1.0.0"` becomes correct, because the major version
then means what semver says it means.

## v0.11.0 — `speed` became an enum

`VideoClip.speed` returned `Double`; it now returns ``Speed``, which makes flat
and curved speed mutually exclusive at the type level rather than by
documentation.

<!-- readme-snippets: skip -->
```swift
// Before
let rate = clip.speed            // Double
```

```swift
// After
switch clip.speed {
case .flat(let rate):
    print("plays at \(rate)x")
case .curved(let animation):
    print("ramps through \(animation.keyframes.count) keyframes")
}
```

## v0.14.0 — three removals

All three were deprecated in v0.11 and are mechanical:

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `VideoClip.speed(_ rate: Double)` | `speed(.flat(rate))` |
| `VideoClip.speed(curve: Animation<Double>)` | `speed(.curved(animation))` |
| `VideoClip.filterAnimation(at: Int, _:)` | ``VideoClip/filterAnimation(for:_:)`` |

Since 1.2, a number literal is a ``Speed`` again, so `.speed(2.0)` written with a
literal compiles unchanged. A rate in a variable still needs `.speed(.flat(rate))`.

The last one is not just a rename. Index-based access drifts the moment a filter
is added or removed; ``FilterID`` is stable across reordering, which is why the
index form was withdrawn rather than kept as a convenience.

`AudioTrack.speed(_:algorithm:)` is a different API and was never deprecated.

## v0.15.0 — platform floor

iOS 17 / macOS 14 / tvOS 17 / visionOS 1, up from iOS 16 / macOS 13 / tvOS 16.

No source change is required if you already target iOS 17. If you need the iOS
16 floor, stay on the `0.14.x` line — it is the last release before the lift.

## The three that compile fine and behave differently

These are the reason this guide exists. Nothing here fails to build.

### v0.16.0 — error text changed

``KadrError`` gained `LocalizedError`, so `error.localizedDescription` changed
observably — from `"The operation couldn't be completed. (Kadr.KadrError error
6.)"` to a sentence written for the person reading it.

**If you match on error strings, that matching breaks.** Switch on the case
instead, which was always the supported approach:

<!-- readme-snippets: skip -->
```swift
// Fragile before, broken now
if error.localizedDescription.contains("error 6") { ... }
```

```swift
// Correct
do {
    let file = try await video.export(to: outputURL)
    print(file)
} catch KadrError.invalidTransition(let reason) {
    print(reason)   // e.g. a transition longer than a clip it joins
}
```

If you *display* `localizedDescription`, you get better text for free — and
should also surface `recoverySuggestion`, which `localizedDescription` does not
include and which carries the actionable half of most messages.

### v0.18.0 — filter identities survive appends

Before v0.18, `.filter(_:)` regenerated **every** ``FilterID`` on the clip each
time a filter was appended. An animation bound with `filterAnimation(for:)` was
silently orphaned by the next `.filter(_:)` call.

That is now fixed: appending extends the id array instead of rebuilding it.

**If you worked around the old behaviour** — re-reading ids after every append,
or re-binding animations defensively — that code is now unnecessary. It is not
harmful, but it is the kind of workaround worth deleting while you remember why
it existed.

### v0.20.0 — a bitrate on a single image clip now takes a different path

``Video/quality(_:)`` is new, so this affects nobody upgrading. It is listed
because the behaviour is surprising in isolation: a composition of one
``ImageClip`` normally takes a fast path straight to the image encoder, and
setting an explicit quality deliberately disqualifies that path so the bitrate
can be honoured. The export is slower and produces the file you asked for.

## What 1.0 promises

No breaking change without a major version bump. The surface frozen at v0.14 is
the surface 1.0 commits to.

Additions will continue as minors. A `1.x` release may add API; it will not
remove or change the meaning of what is here.

## See Also

- ``Speed``
- ``FilterID``
- ``KadrError``
- <doc:FrameAccuracy>

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/MultiTrackComposition.md -->

# Multi-Track Composition

Putting clips beside each other in time rather than after each other.

## Overview

By default, clips in a ``Video`` builder chain: each starts where the previous one
ended. That is the right model for a cut sequence and the wrong one for anything
layered — a picture-in-picture, a watermark clip, a reaction inset.

Two constructs break the chain, and which one to reach for depends on whether you
are placing *one* clip or *several*.

## One clip, placed by time

``VideoClip/at(time:)-(TimeInterval)`` pins a clip to an absolute composition time. It leaves the
chain — the clips around it behave as though it were not there:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: main).trimmed(to: 0...10)     // the spine
    VideoClip(url: inset).trimmed(to: 0...3)
        .at(time: 2.0)                            // floats above it
        .transform(Transform(center: .topRight, scale: 0.3, anchor: .topRight))
}
```

Later clips draw above earlier ones, so declaration order is layer order. Without
a ``Transform`` the inset covers the spine completely, which is almost never what
was wanted — placement and scale usually travel together.

## Several clips, as a group

``Track`` is a parallel sub-timeline. Clips inside it chain among themselves,
while the track as a whole sits at one point in the parent:

```swift
let video = Video {
    VideoClip(url: main).trimmed(to: 0...20)

    Track(at: 2.0) {
        VideoClip(url: a).trimmed(to: 0...3)
        VideoClip(url: b).trimmed(to: 0...3)     // starts when `a` ends
    }
    .opacity(0.8)
}
```

Reach for `Track` when the layered content has its own internal sequence. Reach
for `at(time:)` when it is a single element. Using `at(time:)` on each clip of a
sequence works, but it makes every duration a hand-computed offset — and the
arithmetic breaks the moment one clip's length changes.

## What multi-track costs

A composition with any clip carrying an explicit start time, a `Track`, or a
per-clip transform routes through the multi-track builder, which produces a
video composition with per-clip layer instructions.

That path is measurably more expensive than the simple one — roughly three times
the export time for a four-clip composition in this project's own benchmarks. It
is not a reason to avoid layering, but it is a reason not to reach for
`at(time:)` when a plain chain would do.

## Naming tracks

``Track/init(name:_:)`` takes an optional label. It does not affect rendering; it
exists so a consuming editor can show something meaningful in a timeline UI
instead of *Track 2*.

## See Also

- ``Track``
- ``Transform``
- ``Clip/startTime``
- <doc:CustomCompositors>

<!-- Sources/Kadr/Kadr.docc/Slideshows.md -->

# Building a Slideshow

Turning still images into a video, and the two things that make one watchable.

## Overview

A slideshow is the shortest path from nothing to an exported video: no source
footage, no trimming, no format questions. It is also the composition most likely
to look mechanical, because stills do not move and cuts between them are abrupt.

Two modifiers fix that, and they are the reason this article exists rather than a
one-line snippet.

## The minimum

``ImageClip`` takes an image and a duration. Anything in a ``Video`` builder
chains in declaration order.

```swift
let slideshow = Video {
    ImageClip(first, duration: 3.0)
    ImageClip(second, duration: 3.0)
    ImageClip(third, duration: 3.0)
}
.preset(.reelsAndShorts)

let file = try await slideshow.export(to: outputURL)
```

If you have no images to hand, ``SampleMedia`` generates them:

```swift
let video = Video {
    for index in 0..<4 {
        ImageClip(SampleMedia.image(index: index), duration: 2.0)
    }
}
```

## Making the cuts soft

A hard cut between two stills reads as a glitch rather than an edit. Place a
``Transition`` between clips — it is a clip in the builder, not a modifier on one:

```swift
let video = Video {
    ImageClip(first, duration: 3.0)
    Transition.dissolve(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(second, duration: 3.0)
}
```

A transition cannot start or end a composition, and two cannot sit adjacent —
both throw ``KadrError/invalidTransition(_:)`` with an explanation rather than
failing at export time.

Note that a transition *overlaps* the clips it joins, so the finished video is
shorter than the sum of the durations. Budget for it when the total length
matters.

## Making the stills move

The other half of a watchable slideshow is motion. A slow push or drift — the Ken
Burns effect — is a ``Transform`` animated across the clip's lifetime:

```swift
let push = Animation<Transform>.keyframes([
    .at(0.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.0)),
    .at(3.0, value: Transform(scale: 1.12)),
])

let clip = ImageClip(photo, duration: 3.0)
    .transform(Transform(scale: 1.0), animation: push)
```

Keep the range small. A 12% push over three seconds reads as intent; 50% reads as
a zoom, and on a still image that mostly reveals compression artefacts.

Alternate the direction between slides — push on one, pull on the next — or the
whole sequence acquires a rhythm that draws attention to the technique.

See <doc:KeyframeAnimation> for what else can be driven this way.

## Titles

``TitleSequence`` renders text on a solid background and behaves like any other
clip, so it takes transitions and transforms on the same terms:

```swift
let video = Video {
    TitleSequence("Summer", duration: 2.0)
    Transition.fade(duration: 0.5)
    ImageClip(beach, duration: 3.0)
}
```

## Audio

Background music attaches to the composition rather than to a clip:

```swift
let scored = slideshow.audio {
    AudioTrack(url: musicURL)
        .volume(0.6)
        .fadeIn(1.0)
        .fadeOut(1.5)
}
```

A fade out matters more than it sounds: music that stops dead at the last frame
is the most common way an otherwise finished slideshow feels unfinished.

## See Also

- ``ImageClip``
- ``TitleSequence``
- ``Transition``
- ``SampleMedia``
- <doc:KeyframeAnimation>
